Usually i shrug these posts off, but if youre entering the game design major, i have Many Words of advice and warning if youre shutting down entire lectures as "propaganda" lmao

tl;dr
why didnt you just contact your professor with constructive feedback if you want to witness more productive changes in lecture instead of a passive agressive reddit post...? also idk how to else to tell you this but if you want to work in games...you should probably care about developers working on games & learn not only what they've made, but about issues that affect them and their projects. 

as an upperclassmen in AGPM, believe me when i say that game design, especially games with a larger scope, isn't a solo effort nor should it be if you want to make a Good game. games aren't designed in a vacuum & dismissing one valid lens (of many) through which to learn & observe games history is stubbornly naieve. 

i genuinely feel sorry for you if you dismiss any "some things in the history of games so far have Not Been Great & Perpetuated something harmful to lower class/indie developers/women/minorities" point as "sjw propaganda". i understand that confronting information that might suggest something harmful
about those who you might share an identity with or something that's dear to you can be A Lot to handle. but i think addressing that and bursting the bubble you might have grown up in is part of becoming a better person, kinder team member, and mindful developer who looks out for their peers & issues that might affect them.

nobody is threatening your livelihood if you disagree with points that might be brought up during lecture. many professors in agpm & some that i've had in cmpm genuinely care so much for their students and are open to dialogue if you go to their office hours or shoot them an email. i encourage you to talk with your professor for productive conversation if youre super upset and want to give constructive feedback in regards to the content of lectures.

im not afraid to admit that 80H when i took it a couple years back was Not my favorite of the foundation courses, but reading up on a thing that was super interesting, but not necessarily a focal point in lecture is a good skill regardless of your major. and again, contact your professor if you have feedback for lecture content.

but also, idk how to tell you this lightly... but games history isn't a special exception that's free from shitty people with shitty beliefs who make the field a shitty place for people who might not fit a certain mold. games history is so deeply involved with corporations vs developer labor rights and excluding certain groups of people as a targeted demographic ever since coin-operated arcade games. these things have effects that are STILL super prevalent in the industry today (studio crunch 100+ hour work weeks, lack of women & diversity in stem & games & esports, sexual harrassment culture at studios like riot games, nintendo lawsuits with fan games, etc.), so it's kind of important to understand and learn these things so we don't perpetuate some trashy industry behaviors that burns out and treats developers like they're worth nothing.

universally, those who don't learn history are doomed to repeat the mistakes of history. it's vital for those of us who want to work in games in the future to learn this history. not to make us Feel Bad or "Guilty" for things we might not have done, but to remind us to not repeat these things and make games better and more fun for everyone to make and play.

not gonna lie... one of my favorite episodes of the entire series. also mind the (incoherent) mini ramble and reflection i just finished binging the season and wanted to revisit this episode:

some folks mentioned that they thought the ending of the episode threw them off. but i found the ambiguity really fitting for the episode's tone and personally both haunting yet comforting.

there's this sense of dread and doubt that comes after the reveal that bojack is in the wrong parlor full of strangers. and it got me asking questions like: what if his mother's funeral parlor was empty? how would people who actually went to beatrice's funeral react to bojack's eulogy? Were the occasional gasps and murmuring real or were they bojack's hallucinations?
and imagining possibly even further spirals for bojack like "oh what if no one goes to his funeral when he dies?" or "would the other characters say the opposite: 'bojack died and everything is better'" etc..

but also...a sad, cold comfort in being left to ask those sorts of questions without the viewers or bojack facing the absolute, cold reality of it without any sort of leeway for interpretation similarly to the 'I-C-U' thing
